page: Microsoft Azure M32ls is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The platform utilizes a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor based on x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at an operational clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Hardware memory resources include 256.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Storage is integrated directly via a bundled 1100 GB local SSD. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate stable multi-core capabilities juxtaposed with limited single-threaded efficiency. In multi-threaded evaluations, the M32ls performs within the middle 50% benchmark tier, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 8551.0, a PassMark CPU score of 21054.01, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 106.6 GB/sec. Real-world transactional tests show balanced output, recording 20.68 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations rating of 8766.36. Conversely, single-core processing sits in the bottom 10% bracket, with a single-core Geekbench score of 912.0 and reduced compression throughput, reflecting the constraints of this CPU generation under serialized loads.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the M32ls prioritizes high memory capacity and local high-capacity storage over high clock speed execution. The hardware configuration makes the server appropriate for memory-resident datasets, caching clusters, and relational database management systems that benefit from dedicated core allocations and large RAM density. Workloads demanding rapid single-thread execution, modern vector instruction extensions such as AMX, or specialized hardware acceleration are not compatible with this instance profile.
description: Microsoft Azure M32ls is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor running at 2.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Engineered for memory-intensive enterprise demands, it provides 256.0 GB of RAM alongside a 105 MB L3 cache and a bundled 1100 GB local SSD, without GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles place its multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth (106.6 GB/sec read), and transactional throughput in the middle performance tier, highlighted by 20.68 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 10%, indicating a clear trade-off between parallel throughput and single-thread execution speed. The server is well matched for memory-bound tasks, in-memory caches, and database management workloads that require generous memory allocation and local scratch storage over high clock-speed capabilities.
